messages:
sam: noticing a 1.8-2.2x p95 token latency regression on mixtral/qwen workloads since the triton runtime bump. canary traffic shows it clearly. rolling canary back now :grimacing:

deploy-bot: rollback started for canary cluster (canary-42) by sam at 2026-03-18T10:12:36Z :wrench:

anya: I ran a tiny microprofile against the canary image. summary: flashattention path is being skipped for head_dim=40 and 52 on a few models (mixtral-8x, qwen-7b). selector falls back to SDPA which is ~2.2-2.5x slower per token. KV cache hit path is fine — the extra cost is from kernel choice at attention compute.

kevin: do you have the raw numbers?

anya: paste of the perf run (sanitized):
```
model: mixtral-8x, seq=2048, batch=1, head_dim=40
kernel=flash(triton) chosen: NO -> reason: head_dim % 16 != 0
kernel=sdpa chosen: YES
tokens/sec: 320
token_latency(ms): 3.12
kernel=sdpa: avg 7.1ms per token (attention)
kernel=reference: avg 14.3ms per token
```

anya: and for head_dim=64 on same HW:
```
model: mixtral-8x, seq=2048, batch=1, head_dim=64
kernel=flash(triton) chosen: YES
tokens/sec: 760
token_latency(ms): 1.31
```

kevin: hmm so the selector logic is still enforcing alignment restrictions (8/16) and Triton's optimized flash kernel only reports safe behavior for multiples. might be the triton patch tightened heuristics.

dina: I reproduced a masking oddity when seq > 4096 on qwen with head_dim 52 — saw some attention scores with extreme negative values then a spike in runtime memcopy errors. logs: "compute_mask: out-of-bounds mask index" followed by burst of retries. could be related to our masking vectorization assuming 16-wide lanes.

anya: yes that lines up. our current fallback path is SDPA, which handles odd dimensions but is much slower. two things to consider: (1) a cheap pad-until-8 shim that pads head dim on the GPU path so flash can be used, or (2) a Triton fallback kernel that handles unaligned dims but is optimized (chunked flash with remainder loop).

oliver: ++ to building a chunked/triton-flash remainder path. pads are easiest short-term but can increase memory and KV cache alignment complexity (you have to pad KV rows consistently, and that interacts with our prefix cache).

sam: telemetry shows increased memory churn and slightly higher cache misses during the canary period. pad strategy might increase memory but reduce compute time; tradeoff analysis needed. can we quantify extra memory per request?

anya: rough calc: padding from 40->48 adds 20% to per-head state. for mixtral-8x with 64 heads that's ~0.2 * head_state. on a 32GB GPU with batch=1 seq=2048, this is ~200MB extra worst-case. transient but knobs for pad_threshold could help (only pad when seq<some limit or when memory headroom exists).

kevin: For safety we should also add a masking validation unit test to catch the "compute_mask" OOB when head_dim not multiple of vector lanes. Add fuzzed seq lengths around 512/1024/2048/4096/8192.

anya: opened a quick PR locally: kernel_selector: add policy "force_chunked_flash_for_unaligned_heads" (default false). also a runtime flag to enable pad-to-multiple-of-8. PR includes microbench harness and perf numbers. will push soon.

oliver: I'll work on a Triton kernel variant that handles remainder lanes without calling generic SDPA. plan: implement kernel with main vectorized loop (16-wide) + scalar tail loop, test correctness against fp32 golden. should give ~1.1-1.4x slower than aligned flash but much better than SDPA.

dina: repro command I used to trigger mask OOB: 
```
./run_infer --model=qwen-7b --backend=triton --seq=8192 --batch=1 --heads=52 --head-dim=52 --kv-cache
```
logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T10:05:12Z] compute_mask: idx=8192 mask_end=8188 -> OOB
[2026-03-18T10:05:12Z] attention_kernel: fallback=sdpa (reason=mask_oob)
[2026-03-18T10:05:12Z] runtime: retrying kernel, latency spike observed
```

sam: good repro steps. change plan: pause canary until we have either pad-until-8 shim enabled by default or the chunked triton kernel merged. prefer chunked kernel long-term. in the short term enable pad policy behind an env var for affected customers.

infra-bot: perf job queued: job/eng-runtime/flash-unaligned-profiles-1870123456 -> https://ci.internal/jobs/1870123456/results

kevin: I'll add unit tests to the masking suite and a new microbench target that sweeps head_dim in [32..80] non-multiples to catch regressions. Also add telemetry metric: kernel_path_selected with head_dim tag.

anya: PR pushed to draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/kernel-selector/pulls/889 (includes pad shim + microbench). perf numbers attached in PR description.

oliver: once I have kernel variant I'll link a branch. expect basic correctness PR by EOD local time. I'll try to reuse our existing kernel autotune infra so we get perf profiles automatically.

sam: assign owners: anya (short-term pad + tests), oliver (triton remainder kernel), kevin (tests + telemetry). keep me posted in this thread. canary remains paused until green from perf and masking tests. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary rollback completed for canary-42 at 2026-03-18T10:16:18Z.

sam: thanks all, let's sync again after the chunked kernel PR lands and the perf job finishes.
